title: Who's Viewing This Page
summary: Count distinct recent page viewers with expiring presence state and geographically local heartbeats.
narrative:
Design a system that lets users know the number of other users currently viewing a page, such as a hotel site showing '12 people are looking at this hotel'. Here, 'current' means active within the last 5 minutes, so a closed tab may linger until that window expires. Send a heartbeat on page open and every ~30 s while it remains open. Use a stable user id, or an anonymous session id, so reloading does not count the same viewer twice; subtract the caller's own membership when displaying other viewers.

At ~5 M concurrent viewers across ~10 M pages, heartbeats generate ~5 M / 30 ≈ 170 K updates/s. At ~50 B per entry, 5 M entries occupy ~250 MB before sorted-set overhead and replication; recently departed viewers add state within the 5-minute window. Geo-route clients with DNS to the nearest region, then balance heartbeats across redundant Web Servers. In Cache, update a per-page sorted set with ZADD page:{id} now userOrSessionId, trim scores at or before now minus 5 minutes with ZREMRANGEBYSCORE, and return ZCARD in the heartbeat response. Execute update, trim and count atomically for a coherent local result; expire abandoned page keys with a TTL.

Keep presence entirely in geographically replicated caches; long-term view analytics belongs to a separate system. Replicate each region's presence cache so one node failure does not erase every count. Merge regional counts asynchronously; geo-routing keeps each viewer in one region, so summing regional counts (or merging HyperLogLogs) rarely double counts, and a few seconds of staleness or a slightly incorrect count is acceptable. For very hot pages, merge minute-bucket HyperLogLogs for an approximate distinct count with bounded window-boundary error. Optionally push count changes through WebSocket Servers reading the same caches, and monitor heartbeat failures and stale counts.

functional: Send a heartbeat on open and every ~30 s; return the recent viewer count in each response
Maintain per-page sorted sets of stable user/session ids and last-seen timestamps in Cache
Atomically refresh membership, trim entries older than the 5-minute window and count remaining viewers
Exclude the caller's own membership from the displayed number of other viewers; expire abandoned page keys
Geo-route users and merge regional counts asynchronously with identity-aware deduplication
nonFunctional: Sustain ≈170 K heartbeat updates/s across regions
Tolerate brief staleness and approximate global counts
Survive one Web Server or presence Cache node failure
constraints: Keep heartbeat presence ephemeral in Cache; do not write it to SQL or NoSQL
Use stable viewer identities across reloads and trim individual timestamps; a key TTL alone does not expire members
Keep durable view analytics separate from this presence service
capacity: ~5 M concurrent viewers across ~10 M pages; ~30 s heartbeat interval → ≈170 K updates/s
~50 B per entry × 5 M entries ≈250 MB before overhead and replicas; the 5-minute tail adds recently departed viewers
Presence window: 5 min; asynchronously merged counts may be stale for a few seconds
specs.tradeoff: Sorted sets retain viewer identities for deduplication and a precise local time window at a memory cost. Minute-bucket HyperLogLogs bound memory on hot pages but estimate distinct viewers and introduce bucket-boundary error. Regional caches reduce heartbeat latency while asynchronous merging weakens global freshness.
specs.bonus: Connect Client → WebSocket Server → Cache for pushed count changes, and add Monitoring for heartbeat failures and presence freshness.

hints: Start with Client → DNS for regional routing and Client → Load Balancer → Web Server for heartbeats. Use stable viewer ids and a 5-minute last-seen window.
Connect Web Server → Cache for per-page sorted sets. Atomically refresh a timestamp, trim expired members and count; add key TTLs for abandoned pages. Keep heartbeat writes out of databases.

Run two Web Servers and two Cache nodes; connect each Web Server to both caches. For push, add Client → WebSocket Server and WebSocket Server → both caches. Connect each Web Server → Monitoring. The heartbeat response still supports pull counts.
tips: A simple distributed key-value cache (accommodation_id → count) with an increment is a start, but "current" viewers means views within the last 5 minutes, so counts must also go down.
Store user ids with timestamps rather than a bare counter, so a user who keeps reloading the page is not counted twice; entries older than 5 minutes must drop out of the count.
Replicate the cache geographically; consistency is not a requirement, and a slightly incorrect count can be tolerated for a short time.
Persistent storage is probably unnecessary: the counts are temporary, and long-term view tracking belongs to a separate system.
